title: 2000 AMC 10 Problem 10
statement: The sides of a triangle with positive area have lengths \(4,\) \(6,\) and \(x.\) The sides of a second triangle with positive area have lengths \(4,\) \(6,\) and \(y.\) What is the smallest positive number that is not a possible value of \(|x - y|?\)

solutions.text:
By the triangle inequality, each of \(x\) and \(y\) can be any number strictly between \(6 - 4 = 2\) and \(6 + 4 = 10.\)

Then \(|x - y|\) can take any value with \(0 \le |x - y| \lt 8.\)

The smallest positive number not attainable is \(10 - 2 = 8.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The triangle inequality forces each of \(x\) and \(y\) to lie strictly between \(2\) and \(10\)
Find the range of \(|x - y|\) when \(x\) and \(y\) each range over that open interval
